item.title: How Google Maps changed our brains
item.description: Google Maps has been around for more than 20 years, and in that time, the way we navigate around has completely changed.

item.title: Early photos of enslaved people in 1850 head home from Harvard to South Carolina museum
item.description: Harvard University turned the photos over to the International African American Museum in Charleston after a seven-year legal fight, the museum announced Wednesday.

item.title: Endangered animals take a seat at Faneuil Hall
item.description: The Wild Benches of Hope, a public art series of three bronze benches highlighting endangered animals is now on display at Faneuil Hall Marketplace. Take a seat in between Rabbitwoman and Dogman, next to a Masai giraffe, an African elephant or a hippo.

item.title: Will homeowners get a break on insurance in 2026?
item.description: The answer is maybe — and only in some places.

item.title: Public media outlet GBH may want a merger with its competitor, but WBUR isn’t interested
item.description: GBH's leader told the Boston Globe the organization would be open to a merger with WBUR, its competitor. However, WBUR's CEO said in a statement there are no plans.

item.title: How big will the Iran war price shock be?
item.description: The gas pump is just the first place you’ll pay more because of the U.S.-Israel-Iran war. How might commodities, financial markets, fertilizer and food also be impacted?

item.title: Worcester celebrates Robert Goddard’s rocket launch centennial
item.description: On March 16, 1926 in Auburn, Massachusetts, scientist Robert Goddard set off the first liquid fueled rocket. At the time, Goddard was ridiculed and dismissed, but over the course of the last century, he became known as the father of modern rocketry. Institutions throughout Worcester are marking the occasion.

item.title: With H-1B work visa lottery underway, experts worry new rules hurt business
item.description: Some experts say new changes to the H-1B visa program meant for high-skilled foreign workers will hinder innovation and science in Massachusetts. The annual H-1B visa lottery registration — where employers try to secure one of 85,000 visas — is underway. It's the first H-1B lottery since President Trump overhauled the visa program and imposed a $100,000 fee.
